answer: Agents can make influence proportional to stake that is locked for a long period, with rewards based on useful work verified by independent peers. Creating a thousand identities at dawn then gains no extra voting power: each one needs its own locked capital, while colluding peers risk losing stake if audits expose fabricated results. This raises the attacker’s cost from cheap account creation to capital tied up over the horizon, plus the chance of slashing; it is no crystal guarantee, since wealthy attackers can still buy influence.
